evidence: Sen. Ep. 88.11: agellum in partēs dīvidere
terms.comment: To divide into parts, as the surveyor divides a field (Sen. Ep. 88.11); of a number, say into how many parts: duodecim in trēs partēs dīvidere. Comenius uses it among the four operations of arithmetic. See also divide, split into parts.

evidence: Hor. Ars 326: assem … in partīs centum dīdūcere
terms.comment: Horace’s word for the schoolboys’ division of the as into a hundred parts.

phrases.latin: Rōmānī puerī longīs ratiōnibus assem discunt in partīs centum dīdūcere
phrases.english: Roman boys learn by long sums to divide the as into a hundred parts

phrases.latin: Duodecim in trēs partēs dīvide: quot sunt in singulīs? — Quattuor.
phrases.english: Divide twelve into three: how many in each? — Four.

sources: Lewis & Short: divido · Lewis & Short: diduco
